core_obligations: Reduce rationally equivalent cycles to divisors of rational functions: write an element alpha of Z_k(X) rationally equivalent to zero as a locally finite sum of pushforwards (i_j)_* div(f_j), form the disjoint union W of the integral W_j, note that pi : W -> X is finite, and use the finite pushforward statement for K_0 to reduce to W, hence to X integral of delta-dimension k + 1 (proof lines 3948-3961).

In the integral case, let I be the ideal of denominators of the rational function f and use the two short exact sequences 0 -> I -> O_X -> O_X/I -> 0 and 0 -> I -> O_X -> O_X/fI -> 0: show that the claim [O_X/I]_k - [O_X/fI]_k = div(f) forces the class of div(f) in K_0(Coh_{<=k}(X)/Coh_{<=k-1}(X)) to be represented by [O_X/I] - [O_X/fI], which maps to zero in K_0(Coh_{<=k+1}(X)/Coh_{<=k-1}(X)) (proof lines 3963-3992).

Prove the claim by comparing coefficients at the generic point of an integral closed subscheme Z of dimension k: the coefficient of [Z] in div(f) is ord_A(f) with A = O_{X,xi}, while the coefficient in [O_X/I] - [O_X/fI] is length_A(A/I) - length_A(A/fI); the distance function turns the latter into d(A,I) - d(A,fI) = d(I,fI) = ord_A(f) (proof lines 3994-4016).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to X integral of dimension k + 1 through the finite covering by the integral schemes W_j (proof lines 3948-3961).
Build the two short exact sequences from the ideal of denominators and show the claim implies the theorem (proof lines 3963-3992).
Compare the coefficients using the distance function (proof lines 3994-4016).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical map from CH_k(X) to K_0(Coh_{<=k+1}(X)/Coh_{<=k-1}(X)) by showing that the cycle-to-K_0 map descends through rational equivalence (statement lines 3933-3945, tag 0FDS). The proof has to unwind rational equivalence into a finite cover by the integral subschemes carrying the divisors, and then, on an integral X of dimension k + 1, produce the ideal of denominators of the rational function and the two short exact sequences of coherent sheaves whose class difference represents the divisor; the final coefficient comparison needs the distance function to turn the difference of two lengths into the order of the function. Each step is a concrete construction, so the claim is H2.
